tiku_evidence: The Aceh queen personally reconfirms a toll EXEMPTION for one VOC ship trading at Tiku (among 4 ports)

proposed_future_review: Recommend a future Draft V2 revision consider whether COLLECTS_TOLL_FROM should carry an explicit boolean/enum sub-field for exemption-vs-collection, or whether a dedicated relation type is warranted for toll exemptions specifically
notes: Directly parallel in kind to Koto Tangah's own T-01 finding (bare institutional-presence facts not cleanly representable) -- both are cases where Draft V2's relation vocabulary is one level too coarse for a specific commercial-instrument nuance.

representation_result: Each period carries its own distinct claim_or_effective_control value (COMMERCIAL_CONTROL, CLAIM, FORMAL_ACCEPTANCE, MILITARY_PRESENCE, UNKNOWN_EFFECTIVE_CONTROL) -- no single relation spans more than 25 years (validator check 29) and no relation asserts continuous effective control across the whole 115-year span

representation_result: No single bridging 'ACTOR_TIKU_1625_1740' research construct was created (unlike Koto Tangah's own coastal-collective bridge) -- each dated point uses its own distinct, narrowly-bounded actor (or no actor, e.g. 1625 and the toll-exemption context), and ACTOR_PONGELOUS_12_DESA_TICCO_1662 is explicitly NOT merged with ACTOR_TIKU_REGENTS_1684 despite both being Tiku-area collectives

proposed_future_review: Recommend the same future researcher decision flagged for Koto Tangah T-14: whether Draft V2 should define a continuity_status field or a distinct actor subtype for research-construct bridging actors -- this artifact deliberately avoided even attempting such a bridge, which is itself informative: TWO genuinely distinct local collectives (1662, 1684) span the timeline rather than one persisting community, unlike Koto Tangah where a single bridging construct was attempted
notes: IMPORTANT CROSS-CASE FINDING: Koto Tangah's T-14 ACTOR_IDENTITY_FAILURE recurs here, but in a DIFFERENT form -- Koto Tangah's failure was about how to represent an attempted continuity bridge; Tiku's failure is that Draft V2 provides no field to explicitly mark 'these two collectives are NOT the same, and this artifact makes that determination as a researcher judgment call, not as a settled ontology property.' Both point to the same underlying gap: Draft V2's Identity Rules (section 4) have no continuity/non-continuity field at all, for either direction of the judgment.
